body: Read as: the git mark is a click target for the facts box, and it sat in the right margin next to the state marks, so the margin stopped meaning one thing. My reading: the margin answers one question, does anything need me, and git does not answer it. So git facts and their mark move left, right after the window label they describe, and the margin keeps state only. That is mockups-rail/v7, compare it against v5 side by side in the strip. The alternative I did not take: show the mark only on a dirty row, so a clean window has no target and the rail loses one glyph per row. Say if you prefer that and I will draw it as v8.
mockups-rail/v7: git stats and the git mark sit after the window label, the aligned state column at the right margin carries state only. Same 22 rows, same rollup.
no value in the yellow dot for git, remove it and keep only the git box

Agreed, and the dot goes in every shape, not only this one. A row that already prints +12 -3 in green and red does not need a third mark for the same fact, and the facts box has its own state row. mockups-rail/v8 is v7 with the dot removed; the counts and the mark stay. One case needs a rule: a tree whose only change is a binary file has no line counts, so it would have read dirty by the dot alone. On that row the file count takes the dot's place, for example 2 files in the dim tone, so a dirty tree is never silent. If you would rather keep the dot for that case only, say so and it becomes a dot that appears only when it is the only evidence.

mockups-rail/v8: window rows lose the dirty dot; +A -D in green and red carries dirty, the git mark stays the facts box target, and a binary-only change falls back to the file count so nothing reads clean by accident.

body: Agreed: a question mark where the state belongs reports the rail's ignorance, not the pane's condition, and silence says the same thing without a glyph. mockups-rail/v9 is v8 with the unknown mark removed. One consequence worth naming: the rollup follows the same rule, so a window or workspace mark is the worst state among its panes and unknown does not win that comparison; a group whose panes are all unknown shows nothing rather than a question mark one level up. In the pip strips of A and C an unknown pane is absent, so three panes with one silent shows two pips. A shell keeps its triangle, because a shell is a fact, not an unknown.
mockups-rail/v9: the unknown state paints nothing at any level. Compare v8 against v9 to see the single glyph that goes.
